summary: NODIXHI is an interactive web tool for exploring the sky and comparing infrared observations. Users can browse stars and celestial objects, choose a SPHEREx band, and blink between available observations to look for changes. By combining real astronomical data with an accessible sky experience, NODIXHI helps users understand how repeated observations can support the search for moving objects.
details:
NODIXHI connects an interactive sky map with a SPHEREx image viewer. Users can explore celestial objects and featured targets, then open the viewer to inspect infrared observations by band. When observations are available for a selected target, the viewer loads real SPHEREx data and lets users compare epochs. This makes the idea behind repeated-sky surveys more tangible: an object that changes position or brightness across observations may deserve a closer look. The project is an educational exploration tool, not a claim that Planet Nine or another new object has been discovered.

Detailed Description:

SPHEREx Sky Viewer is an interactive web application designed to explore NASA SPHEREx mission infrared sky imagery. The project allows users to enter coordinates or object names, select SPHEREx wavelength bands (D1–D6), and compare multiple observation epochs to detect moving or changing celestial objects such as asteroids, brown dwarfs, variable stars, and high proper motion stars. The project uses real data from NASA/IPAC IRSA, along with Gaia DR3 and SIMBAD information, and features a WiseView-style blink viewer that helps users spot differences between image epochs.

Objective:

- Create an accessible and interactive tool for exploring real astronomical data

- Help identify objects that move or change brightness over time

- Make scientific space data easier for the public to understand

- Support education, outreach, and scientific visualization

How the Project Works:

- Users input RA/Dec or a target name

- The system resolves the object using SIMBAD/Gaia data

- The app fetches real SPHEREx images via a local backend proxy

- Data is displayed in multiple modes such as blink, difference mode, stack mode, band selection, and spectrum view

- Users can compare multiple epochs and inspect metadata and overlays

Technologies and Stack:

- Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript

- Backend/Proxy: Python

- Data Sources: NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx, Gaia DR3, SIMBAD, JPL Horizons

- Interfaces: 3D sky scene, interactive map, blink viewer, scientific dashboard

- Data Formats: FITS images, catalog JSON, cached offline demo data

Value and Benefits:

- Easy for non-experts to access space data

- Suitable for education and public engagement

- Enables visual discovery of time-varying astronomical phenomena

- Brings real NASA data into an intuitive, interactive experience

Short Summary:

SPHEREx Sky Viewer is an interactive web platform for exploring NASA SPHEREx infrared data, allowing users to detect celestial objects that move or change brightness by comparing observation epochs. It combines real astronomical data with a user-friendly visual interface to create an engaging educational and scientific experience.

AI is used to accelerate code development and support the team’s workflow, but it does not replace human creativity, scientific reasoning, or decision-making.
